root_cause.text: ksmbd’s SMB ACL construction code stored the cumulative DACL/ACE byte length in 16-bit variables in `set_posix_acl_entries_dacl()` and `set_ntacl_dacl()`, so large ACLs could make the size arithmetic wrap past 65535 and cause subsequent ACE writes to use an already-overwritten buffer offset.
root_cause.evidence: The patch explicitly says “set_posix_acl_entries_dacl() and set_ntacl_dacl() accumulate ACE sizes in u16 variables” and that the accumulated size “can wrap past 65535, causing the pointer arithmetic `(char *)pndace + *size` to land within already-written ACEs”; the fix replaces `*size += ...` and `size += nt_ace_size` with `check_add_overflow(...)` checks before continuing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a local ACE size variable in `set_posix_acl_entries_dacl()` to support subsequent ACL handling logic.
intent_record.what: A new local variable `u16 ace_sz;` was added to `set_posix_acl_entries_dacl()` alongside the existing `sid`, `ntace`, `i`, and `j` declarations.
intent_record.how: This change by itself does not alter runtime behavior in the shown hunk; it prepares the function to track an ACE size value, likely for use later in the function logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent overflow when accumulating ACL ACE sizes while constructing the DACL.
intent_record.what: The code no longer adds the return value of fill_ace_for_sid() directly into *size. Instead, it stores that return value in ace_sz, then calls check_add_overflow(*size, ace_sz, size) and breaks out of the loop if the addition would overflow. The ACE count increment remains after this check.
intent_record.how: This changes the ACE-building loop so that size accumulation is guarded against integer overflow. If adding the newly generated ACE length would overflow the running total, the loop stops instead of wrapping *size to an incorrect value, preventing malformed buffer sizing and potential memory corruption.

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent overflow while accumulating ACL DACL size by checking the ACE size addition before updating the buffer length.
intent_record.what: In the DACL-building loop, the code no longer adds the return value of fill_ace_for_sid() directly into *size. Instead, it stores that return value in ace_sz, then calls check_add_overflow(*size, ace_sz, size) and breaks out of the loop if the addition would overflow.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this change prevents silent integer overflow when accumulating the ACE buffer size. If adding the newly generated ACE size would exceed the representable range, the loop stops instead of wrapping *size to an incorrect value, reducing the risk of building a malformed ACL buffer or overrunning memory calculations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent integer overflow while accumulating ACL ACE sizes during POSIX ACL to DACL conversion.
intent_record.what: The code no longer adds the return value of fill_ace_for_sid() directly into *size. Instead, it stores that return value in ace_sz, then uses check_add_overflow(*size, ace_sz, size) to update *size and breaks out of the loop if the addition would overflow.
intent_record.how: This changes ACL entry construction so that size accounting is protected against integer overflow. If adding the new ACE length to the running total would overflow, the loop stops instead of wrapping the size and continuing with invalid bookkeeping.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add overflow-checked size accumulation in ACL construction to prevent wraparound and malformed output.
intent_record.what: In `set_ntacl_dacl()`, the code that previously advanced `size` with `size += nt_ace_size;` was replaced by a checked addition using `check_add_overflow(size, nt_ace_size, &size)`, and the loop now breaks if the addition overflows.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents `size` from wrapping around on integer overflow while accumulating ACL entry lengths. If the accumulated DACL size would exceed the representable range, the function stops processing instead of continuing with a corrupted offset/length value, reducing the risk of buffer miscalculation and memory corruption.

candidates.rationale: This cumulative size update uses the running DACL byte count without overflow checking. With large ACLs, the 16-bit size can wrap, so later ACE writes use an incorrect offset.
